correctness.rationale: The two-edge lower bound and four-type classification are direct exhaustive structural proofs. Counting uses exactly twelve labelled P4 paths per four-subset. Neighbor degrees count forbidden adjacent P4 triples from each state shape. The all-order three-step bound is reduced rigorously to equivalence relations on twelve endpoint positions and verified over all Bell(12)=4,213,597 patterns; 500,759 valid ordered pairs had paths of length at most three using the union of edges. This finite certificate is exhaustive for every n, not a finite-n conjecture. A disjoint pair forces diameter at least three. Direct independent Kneser adjacency enumeration checks n=5..8; all-source distances checked n=5..7. Open claims are limited to stated n>=5.

value.rationale: The natural isolation/vertex-edge-domination question on the uniform Kneser family gains a full optimum-state classification, an exact multiplicity polynomial, sharp pattern-dependent mobility degrees, and a universal diameter of three. This is not a renamed numerical isolation count: configurations sharing two of three selected edges are adjacent, and the counterexample A={01,02,03}, B={01,14,23} proves a genuine obstruction to Johnson-shortest reconfiguration despite constant diameter. The result informs the structure of optimal sensing or vertex-edge protection configurations across arbitrary ground-set sizes.
